questions.question: Which of these processes begins after pollen lands on the stigma of a flower?

options.text: It develops into a seed directly.
A pollen tube grows through the style to reach the ovary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A pollen tube grows through the style to reach the ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of plant reproduction begins with **pollination**, which is the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** to the **stigma** of a flower.
 
• Once a compatible **pollen grain** lands on the **stigma**, it absorbs moisture and sugar-rich secretions from the stigmatic surface, leading to its **germination**.
 
• During germination, a **pollen tube** emerges from one of the **germ pores** of the pollen grain and grows downward through the internal tissues of the **style**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The **pollen tube** acts as a conduit to transport the **male gametes** (sperm cells) toward the **ovule** located inside the **ovary**.
 
• The growth of the tube is **chemotropic**, meaning it is guided by chemical signals secreted by the **synergid cells** within the **embryo sac**.
 
• Leaves do not begin **photosynthesis** specifically because of pollination; photosynthesis is a continuous metabolic process occurring in **chlorophyll**-containing tissues. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Petals usually **wither** or fall off after successful pollination rather than opening wider, as their primary role of attracting **pollinators** is complete. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Pollen does not develop into a **seed** directly; a seed only forms after the complex process of **fertilization** occurs within the ovule. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Siphonogamy:** This refers to the process in **seed plants** where a **pollen tube** is used to transfer **male gametes** to the **egg cell**, removing the requirement for external water for fertilization.
 
• **Double Fertilization:** A unique feature of **Angiosperms** (flowering plants) where one male gamete fuses with the **egg** to form a **diploid zygote**, and the second male gamete fuses with two **polar nuclei** to form the **triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN)**.
 
• **Structure of the Pistil:** The female reproductive part, or **carpel**, consists of the **stigma** (receptive tip), the **style** (stalk), and the **ovary** (swollen base containing ovules).
 
• **Post-Fertilization Changes:** After successful fertilization, the **ovule** matures into a **seed**, and the **ovary** wall develops into the **pericarp** or the **fruit**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pollen-Pistil Interaction:** This is a dynamic **recognition process** where the **pistil** evaluates the **pollen** to ensure it is "compatible" (belonging to the same species and not self-sterile) before allowing the **pollen tube** to grow.
 
• **Role of Nutrients:** Essential elements like **Boron** and **Calcium** are critical for the successful **germination** and steady elongation of the **pollen tube** through the style.
 
• **Generative and Vegetative Cells:** The pollen grain typically consists of a **vegetative cell** (which forms the tube) and a **generative cell** (which divides to form two **sperm cells**).
</ul

questions.question: When is a neutral salt formed?

options.text: When strong acid reacts with weak base
When weak acid reacts with strong base
When strong acid reacts with strong base

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When strong acid reacts with strong base**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutral salt** is formed when a **strong acid** reacts with a **strong base**. In this chemical reaction, the **hydrogen ions (H+)** from the acid and **hydroxyl ions (OH-)** from the base combine to form **water (H2O)**, leaving behind a salt that has no acidic or basic properties. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• When a **strong acid** reacts with a **weak base**, the resulting salt is **acidic** in nature. This happens because the conjugate acid of the weak base is strong enough to donate protons to water, resulting in a **pH value** of less than **7**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• When a **weak acid** reacts with a **strong base**, a **basic salt** is formed. The conjugate base of the weak acid reacts with water to produce hydroxyl ions, making the solution alkaline with a **pH value** greater than **7**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• When an **acid reacts with a metal**, it generally produces a **salt and hydrogen gas**. While a salt is formed, this specific interaction is categorized as a **single displacement reaction** rather than a standard neutralization reaction intended to define the neutrality of a salt. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **pH** of a **neutral salt** solution, such as **sodium chloride (NaCl)** or **potassium nitrate (KNO3)**, is exactly **7** at **25 degrees Celsius**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**
 
 
• It is a **chemical reaction** in which an **acid** and a **base** react quantitatively with each other.
 
• The general formula is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**.
 
• This reaction is usually **exothermic**, meaning it releases heat energy to the surroundings.
 
 
 
• **Strength of Acids and Bases:**
 
 
• **Strong Acids:** Acids that ionize completely in aqueous solutions, such as **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)**, and **Nitric acid (HNO3)**.
 
• **Strong Bases:** Bases that dissociate completely in water, such as **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)**.
 
• **Weak Acids:** Acids that only partially ionize, like **Acetic acid (CH3COOH)** and **Carbonic acid (H2CO3)**.
 
• **Weak Bases:** Bases that do not ionize fully, such as **Ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH)**.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.
 
• It ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is **neutral**, below 7 is **acidic**, and above 7 is **basic**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Common Examples of Salts:**
 
 
• **Sodium Chloride (NaCl):** Formed from **HCl (Strong Acid)** and **NaOH (Strong Base)**. It is a **neutral salt** used in **food preservation** and as common table salt.
 
• **Ammonium Chloride (NH4Cl):** Formed from **HCl (Strong Acid)** and **NH4OH (Weak Base)**. It is an **acidic salt** used in **dry cell batteries**.
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na2CO3):** Formed from **H2CO3 (Weak Acid)** and **NaOH (Strong Base)**. It is a **basic salt** used in **glass manufacturing** and **water softening**.
 
 
 
• **Salt Hydrolysis:**
 
 
• This is the process where **salt ions** react with **water** to produce acidity or alkalinity. **Neutral salts** derived from strong acids and strong bases do not undergo significant **hydrolysis**, which is why their pH remains **7**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a floral part with its primary biological function in reproduction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stamens – production of pollen grains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stamens** represent the **male reproductive part** of a flower. They are responsible for the **production of pollen grains**, which contain the male gametes necessary for fertilization. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **Pistil** (also known as the **carpel**) is the **female reproductive part**. Its primary biological function is to receive pollen at the **stigma** and house the **ovules** within the **ovary** for fertilization. While it is involved in reproduction, the **attraction of pollinators** is primarily the function of the petals. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sepals** are the outermost green leaf-like structures of a flower, collectively known as the **Calyx**. Their primary function is to **protect the flower** during its **bud stage**. They do not develop **ovules**; ovules develop inside the **ovary** of the pistil. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Petals** are the brightly colored parts of the flower, collectively called the **Corolla**. Their primary function is the **attraction of pollinators** like **insects** and **birds** through their **color** and **scent**. They do not produce **female gametes**; these are produced within the **embryo sac** inside the **ovule**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• A typical flower is organized into **four whorls**: the **calyx**, **corolla**, **androecium** (stamens), and **gynoecium** (pistil).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Stamen:**
 
 
• It consists of two main parts: the **Anther** and the **Filament**.
 
• The **Anther** is a **bilobed** structure where **microsporangia** develop to produce **pollen grains** through the process of **microsporogenesis**.
 
• The **Filament** is a long, slender stalk that supports the **anther** and attaches it to the **thalamus** or **petal**.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Pistil:**
 
 
• The **Stigma** serves as a landing platform for **pollen grains**.
 
• The **Style** is the elongated tube that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**.
 
• The **Ovary** is the basal swollen part containing one or more **ovules** attached to a flattened, cushion-like **placenta**.
 
 
 
• **Pollination and Fertilization:**
 
 
• **Pollination** is the physical transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** to the **stigma**. This can be facilitated by **wind**, **water**, or **biological agents**.
 
• After pollination, the pollen grain germinates, and a **pollen tube** grows through the **style** to reach the **ovule** for **fertilization**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Essential vs. Non-essential Whorls:** The **Androecium** and **Gynoecium** are called **essential whorls** because they are directly involved in **sexual reproduction**. The **Calyx** and **Corolla** are **accessory** or **non-essential whorls** as they assist in protection and attraction.
 
• **Flower Types:**
 
 
• **Bisexual (Hermaphrodite):** Flowers that possess both **stamens** and **pistils**, such as **Lily**, **Rose**, and **Hibiscus**.
 
• **Unisexual:** Flowers that possess either **stamens** (staminate) or **pistils** (pistillate), such as **Papaya**, **Corn**, and **Cucumber**.
 
 
 
• **Post-Fertilization Changes:** After successful fertilization, the **ovule** develops into a **seed**, and the **ovary** matures into a **fruit**. The **petals** and **sepals** often wither and fall off.

questions.question: A small amount of copper oxide taken in a beaker and dilute hydrochloric acid is added to it slowly while stirring, results in:

options.text: formation of reddish-brown colour solution of copper sulphate
formation of reddish-brown colour solution of copper chloride
formation of bluish-green colour solution of copper chloride
formation of reddish-brown colour solution of cupric chloride

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**formation of bluish-green colour solution of copper chloride**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **copper oxide** reacts with **dilute hydrochloric acid**, a chemical reaction occurs that transforms the **black** solid powder into a soluble salt.
 
• **Copper (II) oxide (CuO)** is a **basic oxide**, and its reaction with **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** is a type of **neutralization reaction** (Metal Oxide + Acid → Salt + Water).
 
• The chemical equation for this process is: **CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O**.
 
• The **black colour** of the copper oxide disappears as it dissolves in the acid, and the solution turns **bluish-green**.
 
• This characteristic **bluish-green colour** is due to the formation of **Copper (II) chloride (CuCl2)** in the aqueous solution.
 
• **Statement 1** suggests the formation of a **reddish-brown** solution of **copper sulphate**. This is incorrect because the acid used is **hydrochloric acid**, not sulphuric acid, and copper sulphate typically forms a **blue** solution. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2** suggests a **reddish-brown** colour for **copper chloride**. While copper chloride is formed, its aqueous state is **bluish-green**, not reddish-brown. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 3** states the formation of a **bluish-green** colour solution of **copper chloride**. This accurately describes the visual and chemical result of the reaction. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 4** mentions a **reddish-brown** solution of **cupric chloride**. "Cupric chloride" is another name for **copper (II) chloride**, but the colour description is wrong. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Copper (II) Oxide (CuO):** It is an inorganic compound, often appearing as a **black solid**. It is a **mineral** known as tenorite and acts as a **precursor** to many copper-containing products.
 
• **Copper (II) Chloride (CuCl2):** In its **anhydrous** form, it is **yellowish-brown**, but it commonly exists as a **dihydrate (CuCl2·2H2O)** which is **bright green**. In dilute aqueous solutions, the **copper ions** coordinate with water to produce the **bluish-green** tint.
 
• **Nature of Metal Oxides:** Most **metal oxides** are **basic** in nature. When they react with **mineral acids** like **HCl**, **H2SO4**, or **HNO3**, they form the corresponding **metal salts** and **water**.
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:** This specific reaction is a **double displacement** or **neutralization** where the **hydrogen ions** from the acid combine with the **oxygen** from the oxide to form **water**, while the **metal cation** and **acid anion** form the **salt**.
 
• **Reactivity:** While **copper metal** itself does not react with **dilute hydrochloric acid** because it is below **hydrogen** in the **reactivity series**, its **oxide (CuO)** reacts readily because the reaction is driven by the formation of **water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxidation State:** In this reaction, copper remains in the **+2 oxidation state**. **CuO** is copper (II) oxide, and the resulting **CuCl2** is copper (II) chloride (also known as **cupric chloride**).
 
• **Visual Indicators:** The transition from a **black powder** to a **clear bluish-green liquid** is a definitive **chemical change**.
 
• **Safety:** When performing this in a **laboratory**, stirring is essential to ensure the **black CuO** particles react completely with the **dilute HCl**.
 
• **Product Identification:** If the solution were evaporated, **green crystals** of **copper chloride dihydrate** would be obtained.
</ul

questions.question: Which method is used to purify metals like Zinc and Copper?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electrolytic refining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Electrolytic refining** is a technique used for the **purification** of crude metals to obtain them in a highly pure state. It is the most widely used method for metals like **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Nickel (Ni)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• In this process, a thick block of the **impure metal** acts as the **anode** (the positive electrode), and a thin strip of the **pure metal** acts as the **cathode** (the negative electrode).
 
• A water-soluble salt of the same metal is used as the **electrolyte**. For example, in the refining of **Copper**, acidified **Copper Sulfate (CuSO4)** solution is used as the electrolyte.
 
• When an **electric current** is passed through the electrolyte, the metal ions from the **anode** dissolve into the solution, while an equivalent amount of pure metal from the solution is deposited onto the cathode<

questions.question: Which of the following represents non-uniform linear velocity?

options.text: A ball rolling at uniform rate
A body moving in a straight line at fixed speed
A car moving at constant speed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A train starting from rest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Non-uniform linear velocity** occurs when an object travels in a **straight line** but its **speed changes** over time, or when its **direction changes** while moving. In the case of **linear motion**, the direction remains constant, so non-uniformity arises specifically from a **change in magnitude** (speed).
 
• **A train starting from rest** implies that its initial **velocity** is **zero**. As the train begins to move, it must **accelerate** to gain speed. Because the **magnitude** of its velocity is increasing from **0 m/s** to a higher value, the velocity is not constant. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **A ball rolling at a uniform rate** suggests that the ball is covering **equal distances in equal intervals of time**. If it is rolling in a single direction, both its **speed** and **direction** are constant, representing **uniform velocity**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

questions.question: In India, cows are classified under which scientific species name?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bos indicus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bos indicus**, popularly known as **Zebu** cattle, is the scientific name for the indigenous humped cattle breeds found in **India** and other parts of **South Asia** and **Africa**.
 
• These cattle are distinctively characterized by a prominent **fatty hump** over their shoulders, a large **dewlap** (the fold of skin hanging below the neck), and sometimes drooping **ears**.
 
• The species is highly adapted to the **tropical environment**, showing remarkable resistance to **high temperatures**, **humidity**, and **ectoparasites** such as **ticks**.
 
• Historically, **Bos indicus** is believed to have originated in the **Indian subcontinent** and was domesticated as early as **6000 BCE**.
 
• They are primarily used for **dairy**, **draught power** (ploughing and transport), and **manure** in traditional **Indian agriculture**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Bos indicus.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bos taurus:**
 
 
• This refers to the **humpless cattle** species native to **Europe** and **Northern Asia**.
 
• Common examples include high milk-yielding breeds like **Holstein Friesian**, **Jersey**, and **Brown Swiss**.
 
• Unlike **Bos indicus**, these breeds are best suited for **temperate climates** and are more susceptible to **heat stress** and tropical diseases.
 
 
 
• **Bubalus bubalis:**
 
 
• This is the scientific name for the **Domestic Water Buffalo**, which is a different genus altogether from the cow.
 
• **India** possesses the largest population of water buffaloes in the world, with famous breeds like the **Murrah**, **Surti**, and **Jaffrabadi**.
 
• They are a major source of **milk production** in **India**, contributing significantly to the **White Revolution**.
 
 
 
• **Bos bubalis:**
 
 
• This term is often used as a synonym for **Bubalus bubalis** in older biological texts, though modern taxonomy classifies the water buffalo under the genus **Bubalus**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A2 Milk Significance:** **Indian** indigenous breeds (**Bos indicus**) are known for producing **A2 beta-casein** milk, which is scientifically considered easier to digest and healthier than the **A1 milk** typically produced by **Bos taurus** breeds.
 
• **Major Indian Breeds:** Some of the most notable **Bos indicus** breeds in **India** include the **Gir** (**Gujarat**), **Sahiwal** (**Punjab/Haryana**), **Red Sindhi**, **Tharparkar** (**Rajasthan**), and **Ongole** (**Andhra Pradesh**).
 
• **Draught Breeds:** Breeds like the **Hallikar** and **Amrit Mahal** from **Karnataka** are specifically bred for their immense **physical strength** and endurance in agricultural labor.
 
• **Taxonomic Classification:** Both **Bos indicus** and **Bos taurus** belong to the family **Bovidae** and the subfamily **Bovinae**, under the order **Artiodactyla**.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** To protect these indigenous species, the **Government of India** launched the **Rashtriya Gokul Mission** in **2014** for the conservation and scientific development of **indigenous cattle breeds**.
</ul

questions.question: Momentum (p) is a vector quantity. That means, momentum has both __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**magnitude and direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **vector quantity** is defined in physics as a physical quantity that possesses both a **numerical value (magnitude)** and a **specified direction**.
 
• **Momentum**, represented by the symbol **p**, is the product of an object's **mass (m)** and its **velocity (v)**. Since **velocity** is a vector quantity, the resulting momentum must also be a **vector quantity**.
 
• The **magnitude** of momentum refers to "how much" motion an object has, which depends on how **heavy** the object is and how **fast** it is moving.
 
• The **direction** of momentum is always the same as the **direction** of the object's **velocity**. For example, if a car is moving **North**, its momentum vector is also directed toward the **North**.
 
• In contrast, **scalar quantities** such as **mass**, **time**, and **speed** only have **magnitude** and no direction. ***Hence, the correct answer is magnitude and direction.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SI Unit and Dimensions**:
 
 
• The **Standard International (SI) unit** of momentum is the **kilogram-meter per second (kg·m/s)**.
 
• In terms of dimensional analysis, momentum is expressed as **[M L T⁻¹]**, where **M** is mass, **L** is length, and **T** is time.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**:
 
 
• **Sir Isaac Newton** established that the **force (F)** acting on an object is equal to the **rate of change of its momentum** over **time (t)**.
 
• This relationship is mathematically represented as **F = dp/dt**. If the mass remains constant, this simplifies to **F = ma** (force equals mass times acceleration).
 
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Momentum**:
 
 
• This fundamental principle states that in an **isolated system** where no **external forces** are acting, the **total linear momentum** of the system remains **constant (conserved)**.
 
• This law is crucial in analyzing **collisions** and **explosions**, such as the recoil of a **gun** when a **bullet** is fired.
 
 
 
• **Impulse**:
 
 
• **Impulse** is the change in momentum of an object when a **force** acts upon it for an **interval of time**.
 
• It is also a **vector quantity** and is measured in **Newton-seconds (N·s)**, which is equivalent to **kg·m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Relativistic Momentum**:
 
 
• At speeds approaching the **speed of light (c)**, the classical formula for momentum (p=mv) is modified according to **Einstein's Theory of Relativity** to account for **Lorentz factor** adjustments.

questions.question: For a given wave, if the speed becomes three times and the wavelength becomes three times, the frequency ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**remains the same**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **wave speed (v)**, **frequency (f)**, and **wavelength (λ)** is given by the wave equation: **v = f × λ**. This formula indicates that the speed of a wave is the product of its frequency and its wavelength.
 
• To find the **frequency**, the equation can be rearranged as **f = v / λ**. This shows that frequency is **directly proportional** to the wave speed and **inversely proportional** to the wavelength.
 
• In the given problem, the **speed** of the wave becomes **three times** its original value (3v), and the **wavelength** also becomes **three times** its original value (3λ).
 
• Substituting these new values into the frequency formula: **New Frequency (f') = (3v) / (3λ)**. The numerical factor of **3** in the numerator and denominator cancels out, resulting in **f' = v / λ**.
 
• Since the new frequency **f'** is equal to the original frequency **f**, the frequency **remains the same**. ***Hence, the correct answer is remains the same.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wave Speed (v)**: 
 
 
• It is the distance traveled by a wave per unit of time. The **SI unit** for wave speed is **meters per second (m/s)**.
 
• The speed of a wave is primarily determined by the properties of the **medium** through which it travels (e.g., density, elasticity, or temperature).
 
 
 
• **Wavelength (λ)**: 
 
 
• It is the distance between two consecutive identical points of a wave, such as from **crest to crest** or **trough to trough** in a transverse wave.
 
• The **SI unit** of wavelength is the **meter (m)**. In a given medium, if the frequency increases, the wavelength must decrease to maintain a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Frequency (f)**: 
 
 
• It is the **number of waves** (or cycles) that pass a fixed point in a given amount of time, usually **one second**.
 
• The **SI unit** of frequency is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named after the physicist **Heinrich Hertz**. 1 Hz is equal to **1 cycle per second**.
 
 
 
• **Time Period (T)**: 
 
 
• It is the time taken for one complete cycle of the wave to pass a point. It is the **reciprocal of frequency**, expressed as **T = 1 / f**.
 
• The **SI unit** for the time period is the **second (s)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Source Dependency**: The **frequency** of a wave is determined solely by the **source** of the vibration. Once a wave is generated, its frequency does not change even if it moves into a different medium.
 
• **Medium Dependency**: When a wave enters a different medium (e.g., light traveling from air into glass), its **speed** and **wavelength** change, but its **frequency** remains constant.
 
• **Electromagnetic Waves**: For electromagnetic waves in a vacuum, the speed is a constant denoted by **c** (approximately **3 × 10⁸ m/s**). In this case, **c = fλ**, meaning frequency and wavelength are always perfectly inversely proportional.
 
• **Sound Waves**: In sound, **frequency** is perceived as **pitch**. A high-frequency sound has a high pitch, while a low-frequency sound has a low pitch.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an application of Archimedes’ Principle?

options.text: Calculating buoyant force on a body in fluid
Determining the density of an irregular solid
Measuring electrical resistance of a wire

questions.solution:

questions.question: A science teacher asks students to measure the current through a bulb using an ammeter. What precaution must the students follow?

options.text: Connect the ammeter without a battery
Connect the ammeter in series with correct polarity
Connect the ammeter with reversed polarity
Connect the ammeter in parallel with the bulb

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Connect the ammeter in series with correct polarity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ammeter** is a measuring instrument used to measure the **electric current** in a circuit. To measure the current passing through a component like a **bulb**, the ammeter must be connected in **series** so that the entire current of the circuit flows through it.
 
• The **polarity** of the ammeter is a critical precaution; the **positive terminal** (usually marked **red** or with a **plus sign**) must be connected to the wire coming from the **positive terminal** of the **battery**, and the **negative terminal** (usually **black**) should be directed towards the **negative terminal**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Connecting an ammeter without a **battery** or power source is futile because there is no **Electromotive Force (EMF)** to drive the flow of **electrons**, resulting in a zero reading. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• If an ammeter is connected with **reversed polarity**, the **pointer** in an analog meter will try to move in the opposite direction (below zero), which can cause **mechanical damage** to the needle or provide a negative reading on a **digital multimeter**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Connecting an ammeter in **parallel** with a load (like a bulb) is dangerous because ammeters have **very low internal resistance**. A parallel connection creates a **short circuit**, allowing a massive amount of current to flow through the ammeter, which can **burn the coil** or blow the **internal fuse**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ideal Ammeter Characteristics**:
 
 
• An **ideal ammeter** is defined as having **zero resistance**. This ensures that its inclusion in the circuit does not alter the total **resistance** and, consequently, does not change the **current** it is intended to measure.
 
• In practice, **real ammeters** have a very small but non-zero resistance, which causes a negligible **voltage drop** across them.
 
 
 
• **Galvanometer to Ammeter Conversion**:
 
 
• An ammeter is typically constructed by connecting a **low resistance** wire, known as a **Shunt**, in **parallel** with a sensitive **Galvanometer**.
 
• The **shunt resistance** allows the majority of the current to bypass the delicate galvanometer coil, enabling the measurement of **large currents** without damaging the instrument.
 
 
 
• **Units and History**:
 
 
• The unit of electric current is the **Ampere (A)**, which is one of the seven **SI base units**. It is defined as the flow of **one Coulomb** of charge per **second**.
 
• The instrument is named after the French physicist **André-Marie Ampère**, who made significant contributions to the study of **electromagnetism** in the **1820s**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Voltmeter**:
 
 
• Unlike an ammeter, a **voltmeter** is used to measure **potential difference** and is always connected in **parallel**.
 
• A voltmeter possesses **high resistance** to ensure it draws minimal current from the main circuit, whereas an ammeter requires **low resistance** to allow maximum current through it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Safety Protocols**: Before turning on the power, always verify the **range** of the ammeter. If the current exceeds the **maximum scale deflection**, the device may be permanently damaged.
 
• **Types of Ammeters**: Modern science uses various types, including **Moving Coil Ammeters** (for DC), **Moving Iron Ammeters** (for both AC and DC), and **Digital Ammeters** which use **analog-to-digital converters (ADC)** for high precision.
 
• **Circuit symbols**: In a standard **circuit diagram**, an ammeter is represented by a **circle** with the letter **'A'** inside it, placed in the path of the current flow.

questions.question: If an object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image formed will be:

options.text: between focus and pole, virtual and erect
at the focus, real and diminished
at the centre of curvature itself, real and of the same size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**at the centre of curvature itself, real and of the same size**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at the **centre of curvature (C)** of a **concave mirror**, the image is formed at the **centre of curvature (C)** itself.
 
• The nature of the image formed in this specific position is **real and inverted**.
 
• The **size of the image** is exactly the **same as the size of the object**, meaning the **linear magnification (m)** is **-1**. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• To understand this formation, consider two rays: one ray **parallel to the principal axis** passes through the **Focus (F)** after reflection, and another ray passing through the **Focus (F)** becomes **parallel to the principal axis** after reflection. Both rays meet at **point C**.
 
• If the object is placed **between the focus (F) and the pole (P)**, the image is formed **behind the mirror** and is **virtual, erect, and magnified**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• If the object is placed at **infinity**, the image is formed **at the focus (F)** and is **real, inverted, and highly diminished** (point-sized). *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• If the object is placed at the **focus (F)**, the image is formed at **infinity** and is **real, inverted, and highly magnified**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror:** It is a **spherical mirror** whose reflecting surface is **curved inwards** (towards the center of the sphere). It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays at a single point.
 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the **height of the image (h')** to the **height of the object (h)**, expressed as **m = h'/h = -v/u**. A **negative sign** indicates a **real image**, while a **positive sign** indicates a **virtual image**.
 
• **Uses of Concave Mirrors:** They are widely used in **shaving mirrors** and **makeup mirrors** to see a larger image, by **dentists** to see large images of teeth, and in **solar furnaces** to concentrate sunlight.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, and the **object distance (u)** is always **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Radius of Curvature (R):** The distance from the **pole (P)** to the **centre of curvature (C)**. For spherical mirrors with small apertures, the **Radius of Curvature** is **twice the focal length**, mathematically represented as **R = 2f**.
 
• **Principal Focus (F):** For a concave mirror, it is the point on the **principal axis** where all rays parallel to the axis **actually converge** after reflection.
 
• **Aperture:** The diameter of the reflecting surface of the spherical mirror is called its **aperture**.
 
• **Comparison with Convex Mirror:** Unlike concave mirrors, a **convex mirror** always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image regardless of the object's position.

questions.question: What does the Law of Conservation of Mass state?

options.text: Mass of reactants is always lost
Energy can be converted into mass
Mass of products is always greater

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass remains unchanged in reactions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** states that in an **isolated system**, mass is neither created nor destroyed by **chemical reactions** or **physical transformations**.
 
• According to the law, the **mass of the products** in a chemical reaction must equal the **mass of the reactants**. This means that the total **number of atoms** of each element is preserved throughout the process.
 
• The law was established by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, marking a significant transition from qualitative to quantitative **chemistry**.
 
• Statement (1) suggests that the **mass of reactants** is always lost. This contradicts the principle that matter is conserved and not destroyed. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (2) asserts that **mass remains unchanged** during reactions. This is the fundamental definition of the law, where the total **mass** remains constant before and after the reaction. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Statement (3) mentions that **energy can be converted into mass**. While true in **relativistic physics** and **nuclear reactions**, it does not define the classical Law of Conservation of Mass used in standard chemistry. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement (4) claims that the **mass of products** is always greater. This is impossible under the law as no new matter can be created from nothing. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Antoine Lavoisier**: Known as the **Father of Modern Chemistry**, he used meticulous **experimental methods** and precision **balances** to prove that mass does not change during combustion or other reactions.
 
• **Stoichiometry**: The **Law of Conservation of Mass** is the foundation for **balancing chemical equations**. Since atoms are only **rearranged** and not lost, the coefficients in an equation must ensure the same **number of atoms** on both sides.
 
• **Isolated vs. Open Systems**: In an **open system**, mass might appear to change (e.g., a burning log losing mass as **carbon dioxide** and **water vapor** escape), but in a **closed container**, the total mass remains perfectly **constant**.
 
• **Chemical vs. Physical Change**: The law applies to both. For example, when **10 grams of ice** melts into **liquid water**, the resulting mass is exactly **10 grams**.
 
• **Historical Context**: Before **1789**, many scientists believed in the **Phlogiston theory**, which argued that a substance called phlogiston was released during burning, explaining the apparent loss of weight in some substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mass-Energy Equivalence**: In modern physics, **Albert Einstein** expanded this concept with the formula **E=mc²**, showing that **mass** and **energy** are interchangeable. However, in **ordinary chemical reactions**, the amount of mass converted to energy is so **minuscule** that it cannot be detected by standard instruments.
 
• **Application**: This law is crucial for **industrial chemistry**, **environmental science**, and **pharmacology** to calculate the exact yield of **products** from specific amounts of **raw materials**.
 
• **Year of Discovery**: The formal publication of this law occurred in **1789** in Lavoisier's textbook, "**Traité Élémentaire de Chimie**".

questions.question: When applying the sign conventions for spherical lenses to measure object and image distances, where are all measurements taken from?

options.text: The optical centre of the lens

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The optical centre of the lens**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• For **spherical lenses**, we follow a set of sign conventions called the **New Cartesian Sign Convention** to measure distances.
 
• According to this convention, the **optical centre** (denoted by **O**) of the lens is taken as the **origin** of the coordinate system.
 
• The **principal axis** of the lens is taken as the **X-axis** (horizontal axis) of the coordinate system.
 
• All distances are measured from the **optical centre** of the lens. Distances measured in the direction of **incident light** (usually to the **right** of the optical centre) are taken as **positive**.
 
• Distances measured in the direction opposite to that of the **incident light** (usually to the **left** of the optical centre) are taken as **negative**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Object Distance (u)**:
 
 
• The **object** is always placed to the **left** of the lens.
 
• Since it is measured against the direction of incident light, the **object distance (u)** is always **negative** in both **convex** and **concave** lenses.
 
 
 
• **Image Distance (v)**:
 
 
• For a **real image**, which is formed on the **right side** of the lens, the image distance **v** is **positive**.
 
• For a **virtual image**, which is formed on the **left side** (the same side as the object), the image distance **v** is **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length (f)**:
 
 
• A **convex lens** (converging lens) has a **positive focal length** because its principal focus lies on the **right side**.
 
• A **concave lens** (diverging lens) has a **negative focal length** because its principal focus is considered to be on the **left side**.
 
 
 
• **Height of Object and Image (h and h')**:
 
 
• Distances measured **perpendicularly above** the principal axis are taken as **positive**. Thus, the **object height (h)** is usually **positive**.
 
• Distances measured **perpendicularly below** the principal axis are taken as **negative**. Therefore, the height of a **real and inverted image** is **negative**, while a **virtual and erect image** is **positive**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula**: The relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula: **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**. This formula is valid for all **spherical lenses** in all situations.
 
• **Magnification (m)**: The **linear magnification** produced by a lens is the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**. It is expressed as **m = h'/h**. It is also related to distances as **m = v/u**.
 
• **Power of a Lens (P)**: The **power of a lens** is defined as the reciprocal of its **focal length** in **metres** (**P = 1/f**). The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**. A **convex lens** has **positive power**, and a **concave lens** has **negative power**.
 
• **Comparison with Mirrors**: Unlike lenses where measurements start from the **optical centre**, in **spherical mirrors**, all measurements are taken from the **pole** of the mirror.

questions.question: When is the work done by a force considered negative?

options.text: When the force acts opposite to the direction of displacement
When the force acts in the same direction as displacement

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When the force acts opposite to the direction of displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In physics, **work done** is defined as the product of the component of the **force** in the direction of the **displacement** and the magnitude of this displacement. Mathematically, it is expressed as **W = Fs cos(θ)**, where **θ** is the angle between the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
• **Negative work** occurs when the **force** acts in the **opposite direction** to the **displacement**. In this case, the angle **θ** between the force and displacement is **180 degrees**. Since **cos(180°) = -1**, the work done becomes **W = -Fs**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Positive work** occurs when the **force** acts in the **same direction** as the **displacement**. Here, the angle **θ** is **0 degrees**, and since **cos(0°) = 1**, the work done is **W = Fs**. This happens when you push an object and it moves in the direction of the push. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Zero work** is done when the **force** applied is **zero**. If no force is exerted on an object, no energy is transferred via mechanical means, regardless of the motion. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Work done** is also **zero** when there is **no displacement** (s = 0), even if a massive force is applied. For example, pushing against a stationary wall results in **zero work** because the wall does not move. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Work:** Work is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no direction, even though it is derived from two **vector quantities** (force and displacement). The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**.
 
• **The Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. When **negative work** is done (such as by **friction**), the object's **kinetic energy decreases**, causing it to slow down.
 
• **Examples of Negative Work:**
 
 
• **Frictional Force:** When a block slides on a floor, the **force of friction** acts opposite to the direction of motion, doing **negative work** and dissipating energy as **heat**.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** When an object is thrown **upward**, the displacement is up, but **gravity** pulls **downward**. Thus, gravity does **negative work** until the object reaches its peak.
 
• **Air Resistance:** A parachute falling through the air experiences upward **drag** while moving downward, resulting in **negative work** by the air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Perpendicular Force:** If the **force** is **perpendicular** to the **displacement** (angle **θ = 90 degrees**), the work done is **zero** because **cos(90°) = 0**. A classic example is a **coolie** carrying a load on his head and walking on a horizontal platform; the force (gravity/normal) is vertical, while displacement is horizontal.
 
• **Centripetal Force:** In **uniform circular motion**, the **centripetal force** acts toward the center of the circle, while the **displacement** is tangential (at **90 degrees**). Therefore, the work done by centripetal force is always **zero**.
 
• **Dimensions:** The dimensional formula for work is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as the dimensions for **energy** and **torque**.
 
• **Sign Significance:** The **positive** sign indicates energy is **transferred to** the object, while a **negative** sign indicates energy is **removed from** the object or transferred to the surroundings.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: On increasing the resistance of the wire, the strength of the magnetic field in a solenoid increases.
The magnetic field inside a solenoid carrying current does not depend on the strength of the current.
On increasing the number of turns per unit length in a solenoid, the strength of the magnetic field in the solenoid increases.
The magnetic field lines inside a solenoid are circular.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**On increasing the number of turns per unit length in a solenoid, the strength of the magnetic field in the solenoid increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **solenoid** is a long coil containing a large number of close turns of insulated **copper wire**. When an electric current passes through it, it behaves like a **magnet**.
 
• The **magnetic field strength (B)** inside a long solenoid is given by the formula **B = μ₀ n I**, where **μ₀** is the permeability of free space, **n** is the number of turns per unit length, and **I** is the current.
 
• On increasing the **number of turns per unit length (n)** in a solenoid, the **strength of the magnetic field** produced inside it increases proportionally. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, current is inversely proportional to **resistance (I = V/R)**. If the **resistance** of the wire increases, the **current (I)** decreases, which in turn **decreases** the magnetic field strength. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **magnetic field** inside a solenoid is **directly proportional** to the strength of the **current** flowing through it. If the current increases, the field strength increases. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **magnetic field lines** inside a solenoid are **parallel straight lines**, indicating that the magnetic field is **uniform** at all points inside the solenoid. They are not circular inside; they form a pattern similar to that of a **bar magnet**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Field:** A solenoid consists of a **cylindrical** shape where the wire is wound closely. The field lines outside the solenoid are similar to those of a **bar magnet**, emerging from the **North pole** and entering the **South pole**.
 
• **Uniformity:** The fact that field lines are **parallel straight lines** inside the solenoid is a crucial feature, as it allows for the creation of a **constant magnetic field** in a specific region, which is essential for many scientific experiments and industrial **applications**.
 
• **Electromagnets:** A strong magnetic field produced inside a solenoid can be used to **magnetize** a piece of magnetic material, like **soft iron**, when placed inside the coil. The combination of the coil and the soft iron core is called an **electromagnet**.
 
• **Polarity:** One end of the solenoid acts as a **magnetic North pole**, while the other behaves as a **magnetic South pole**. The polarity can be determined using the **Clock Rule** or the **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**. If the current flows in a **clockwise** direction at an end, that end is the **South pole**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors affecting Magnetic Field:** 
 
 
• **Current (I):** Directly proportional. Doubling the current **doubles** the field.
 
• **Number of Turns (N):** Directly proportional. More turns result in a **stronger** field because the field of each turn adds up.
 
• **Core Material:** Using a **soft iron core** can increase the magnetic field strength by **thousands** of times compared to an air core.
 
 
 
• **Permeability (μ₀):** The constant **μ₀** (permeability of free space) has a value of approximately **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**. This value changes if a material other than air/vacuum is used as the core.
 
• **Comparison:** Unlike a **permanent bar magnet**, the strength of the magnetic field in a solenoid can be **controlled** by changing the current or the number of turns, and its **polarity** can be reversed by changing the direction of the current.

questions.question: Which of the following methods will NOT help in the management of garbage and other wastes produced by humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Landfilling plastics in soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Landfilling plastics in soil**: Plastics are **non-biodegradable** synthetic materials. When they are buried in landfills, they do not decompose for **hundreds of years**. questions.question: Which is the main transport system in animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Circulatory system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **circulatory system**, also known as the **cardiovascular system**, is the primary **transport system** in animals, responsible for moving **nutrients**, **gases**, and **waste products** throughout the body.
 
• It consists of three main components: the **heart** (a muscular pumping organ), **blood** (the transport medium), and **blood vessels** (the network of tubes).
 
• The primary function of this system is to deliver **oxygen** from the respiratory organs to the **tissues** and to transport **carbon dioxide** back for elimination.
 
• It also plays a crucial role in distributing **hormones** secreted by **endocrine glands** to their specific target organs</

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct for benzene?

a. It is a six-membered cyclic carbon compound.
b. It has three single and three double bonds. 
c. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₄.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a and b**__.

**__Key Points__**

 
• **Benzene** is a fundamental **organic chemical compound** and is categorized as the simplest **aromatic hydrocarbon**. It consists of **six carbon atoms** arranged in a planar ring. ***Hence, statement a is correct.***
 
• In its structural representation (known as the **Kekulé structure**), **Benzene** is depicted as having alternating **three single bonds** and **three double bonds** between the carbon atoms. In modern chemistry, these are understood as **delocalized electrons** forming a **resonance hybrid**, where all bond lengths are equal. ***Hence, statement b is correct.***

questions.question: Which of the following is a pure substance consisting of only one type of atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **pure substance** that consists of only **one type of atom** is defined as a **chemical element**.
 
• **Sodium** is a chemical element represented by the symbol **Na** (from the Latin 'natrium') and carries the **atomic number 11**.
 
• Since **Sodium** is composed entirely of atoms that have the same number of **protons** in their nuclei, it meets the criteria of a substance consisting of only one type of atom. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• It is categorized as an **alkali metal** and is located in **Group 1** of the periodic table.
 
• Under standard conditions, it is a **soft, silvery-white**, and highly **reactive metal** that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Air:**
 
 
• **Air** is a **homogeneous mixture** of several different gases rather than a pure substance.
 
• It primarily consists of **Nitrogen (78%)**, **Oxygen (21%)**, **Argon (0.9%)**, and **Carbon Dioxide (0.04%)**. Because it contains different types of molecules and atoms, it is not an element. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Water:**
 
 
• **Water (H2O)** is a **chemical compound** made up of two different elements: **hydrogen** and **oxygen**.
 
• Although it is a pure substance in the sense that it has a fixed chemical composition, it consists of **two types of atoms** bonded together in a **2:1 ratio**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Milk:**
 
 
• **Milk** is a complex **heterogeneous mixture**, specifically classified as a **colloid**.
 
• It contains various substances such as **water, fats, proteins (like casein), lactose (sugar), and minerals**. Since it is a mixture of many different compounds, it does not consist of only one type of atom. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity of Sodium:** **Sodium** is extremely reactive, particularly with **water** and **oxygen**. To prevent accidental reactions, it is typically stored in **mineral oil** or **kerosene**.
 
• **Atomic Structure:** **Sodium** has **11 protons** and **11 electrons**. Its electron configuration is **[Ne] 3s1**, meaning it has **one valence electron** that it easily loses to form a **cation (Na+)**.
 
• **Natural Occurrence:** Due to its high reactivity, **Sodium** is never found as a free element in nature. It occurs abundantly in compounds, the most common being **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, which is **table salt** found in **seawater** and **rock salt** deposits.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** **Sodium** compounds are used in the production of **glass, paper, soap, and textiles**. It is also vital in **biological systems** for maintaining **fluid balance** and **nerve signal transmission** in the **human body**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes autotrophic nutrition?

options.text: It requires digestion of complex substances outside the body.
It depends entirely on consuming other living organisms for food.
It involves making food using carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight.
It involves direct absorption of organic compounds from other organisms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It involves making food using carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Autotrophic nutrition** is a mode of nutrition in which organisms synthesize their own food from simple inorganic substances such as **carbon dioxide** and **water**.
 
• The process primarily utilized by green plants is **photosynthesis**, which requires the presence of **sunlight** and the green pigment **chlorophyll**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• Digestion of complex substances outside the body is characteristic of **saprotrophic nutrition**, common in **fungi** and certain **bacteria**. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Depending on consuming other living organisms for food is known as **heterotrophic nutrition**, which includes **holozoic** nutrition found in animals and humans. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
